title: The Only Ceramic in the World UNESCO Protects — China's Jade-Green Celadon | China Travel Expert
description:
There's exactly one type of pottery that UNESCO lists as world heritage — and it's Chinese. It turns stone and plant ash into the color of jade.

Longquan celadon, from Zhejiang, traces back to around 220 AD and reached its peak in the Southern Song dynasty, when potters mastered the famous "plum-green" and "misty-blue" glazes. In 2009 its traditional firing techniques became the first and only ceramic inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage. The glaze is mixed from clay, feldspar, limestone, quartz and plant ash — recipes handed down within families — then fired again and again at up to 1,310°C. One wrong degree and the jade color never appears.

🧭 Expert Tip: In Longquan town, several kiln workshops let you throw and glaze your own celadon piece in a single day — book a morning slot so it can fire before you leave.
